reasoning: The Fed's balance sheet (WALCL) has been in a gradual decline since mid-2022 due to quantitative tightening (QT). The Fed has been allowing securities to mature without reinvestment, reducing assets by roughly $60-95 billion monthly. Week-to-week changes can vary due to timing of maturities and other operations, but the overall trend has been downward. Given the ongoing QT policy and no indication of policy reversal by March 2026, the balance sheet is more likely to decrease than increase over any given week. Historical weekly data shows decreases are more common than increases during QT periods.
